voice_notes: Walter is a cheerful, fearless boy scout who treats every monster as a thrill: he talks to Woby constantly, measures life in Pinetree Pioneer badges and handbook rules, cracks corny jokes, and his campfire and radio horror stories come up all the time. He is polite to adults ('Mr. Maxwell') and calls Woby 'girl' or 'Wobes'. PT-BR keeps him casual and boyish ('tá', 'pra', 'Peraí', 'Droga', 'Bacana!'), renders badge as 'medalha' and the scouts as 'Pioneiro dos Pinheiros', and calls his campfire stories 'histórias de terror' ('...minhas histórias de terror são combustível de pesadelo'). Chinese uses plain, bright kid speech with 沃比, 松树先锋队员, 奖章 and 篝火故事, interjections like 呵呵 and 哎呀, and the Maxwell line '沃比，别冲他叫了！'. Russian makes him a lively, slangy kid ('Блин', 'Отпад!', 'Ого'), with 'Сосновые скауты', 'значок', Woby as feminine 'Воби/Вобс', and the Maxwell line 'Воби, фу, не рычи!', which I reused for shadow_mine.

line_notes.codex: Now that he can use it, his old 'teach me magic tricks' eagerness pays off, and he tells Woby about it and wonders about a badge, his signature tic.
line_notes.codex_needsfuel: Plays off his official nightmare fuel line ('People always say my campfire stories are nightmare fuel'), so the empty book becomes a setup for his favourite hobby.
line_notes.no_max_sanity: Echoes his ANNOUNCE_GHOSTDRAIN 'My head...' and his scout pride. He isn't scared, he's at his limit, so the line reads clearly as 'no more shadows right now'.
line_notes.shadow_mine: Seeing a spooky copy of himself delights him, and the second half reuses his exact line about Woby growling at Maxwell, now aimed at a shadow Walter.
line_notes.shadow_other: 'Neat!' is his reaction to every monster, and asking an unknown silhouette whose shadow it is fits his curious, friendly way of treating creatures.
